chunks: Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir عليه السلام said:

“Ghusl (ritual bath) is in seventeen occasions: the night of the seventeenth of the month of Ramadan, the night of the nineteenth, the night of the twenty-first, and the night of the twenty-third, in which Laylat al-Qadr is hoped for; the ghusl of the two Eids; when you enter the two sanctuaries; the day you enter into ihram; the day of visitation; the day you enter the House; the day of Tarwiyah; the day of ʿArafah; when you have washed a deceased person and shrouded him, or touched him after he has become cool; the day of al-Jumuʿah; and the ghusl of the eclipse, when the whole disc is obscured and you awaken and have not performed the salat (prayer), then you must perform ghusl and make up the salat (prayer). And the ghusl of janabah is obligatory.”

key_terms.الزِّيَارَةِ: the day of visitation in the pilgrimage context
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: major ritual impurity requiring obligatory ghusl
key_terms.الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, for which a recommended ghusl is indicated
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: the two sacred sanctuaries, Makkah and al-Madinah
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two Eid festivals, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath prescribed for specific acts and occasions
key_terms.الْكُسُوفِ: the eclipse, specifically when the full disc is obscured
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: the Night of Decree, especially sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What are the seventeen occasions for ghusl according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith lists seventeen occasions on which ghusl (ritual bathing) is prescribed, covering sacred nights in Ramadan, major devotional times, hajj-related rites, contact with the deceased, Jumuʿah, and eclipse prayer circumstances. It concludes by distinguishing ghusl al-janabah as obligatory, showing the legal importance of ritual purity in acts of worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.172 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:

'There are seventeen occasions for ghusl (ritual bathing): on the night of the 17th of the month of Ramadan, the night of the 19th, the night of the 21st, and the night of the 23rd—on which Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree) is hoped for. Also, ghusl on the two Eid’s (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha), upon entering the two holy sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), on the day of putting on the ihram (for pilgrimage), the day of visiting (the sacred sites), the day of entering the House (the Kaaba), the day of Tarwiyah (the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah), the day of Arafah (the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah), after washing a deceased person and shrouding them, or if you touch the deceased after their body has cooled.
There is also ghusl for Jumu’ah, for a solar eclipse if the entire disc of the sun is obscured, and if you wake up and have not prayed, then you must perform ghusl and make up the prayer. Ghusl for janabah (ritual impurity from sexual discharge) is obligatory.'"
